title: Weather Type in Each Country
statement:
Two tables describe countries and their daily temperatures:

- `Countries(country_id, country_name)`: one row per country; `country_id` is unique.
- `Weather(country_id, weather_state, day)`: the temperature `weather_state` (an integer in degrees Celsius) measured in a country on a `day`; `(country_id, day)` is unique and every `country_id` exists in `Countries`.

Classify each country's weather in **November 2019** using the average `weather_state` of its readings from that month:

- `'Cold'` when the average is at most 15,
- `'Hot'` when the average is at least 25,
- `'Warm'` otherwise.

Report the columns `country_name` and `weather_type`. Countries with no reading in November 2019 are left out. Rows may come in any order.
constraints: weather_state is an integer (degrees Celsius) and may be negative
reference:
WITH november AS (
  SELECT country_id, AVG(weather_state) AS avg_state
  FROM Weather
  WHERE day BETWEEN '2019-11-01' AND '2019-11-30'
  GROUP BY country_id
)
SELECT
  c.country_name,
  CASE
    WHEN n.avg_state <= 15 THEN 'Cold'
    WHEN n.avg_state >= 25 THEN 'Hot'
    ELSE 'Warm'
  END AS weather_type
FROM november AS n
JOIN Countries AS c
  ON c.country_id = n.country_id;
brute:
SELECT c.country_name, 'Cold' AS weather_type
FROM Countries AS c
WHERE (SELECT AVG(w.weather_state) FROM Weather AS w
       WHERE w.country_id = c.country_id AND YEAR(w.day) = 2019 AND MONTH(w.day) = 11) <= 15
UNION ALL
SELECT c.country_name, 'Hot'
FROM Countries AS c
WHERE (SELECT AVG(w.weather_state) FROM Weather AS w
       WHERE w.country_id = c.country_id AND YEAR(w.day) = 2019 AND MONTH(w.day) = 11) >= 25
UNION ALL
SELECT c.country_name, 'Warm'
FROM Countries AS c
WHERE (SELECT AVG(w.weather_state) FROM Weather AS w
       WHERE w.country_id = c.country_id AND YEAR(w.day) = 2019 AND MONTH(w.day) = 11) > 15
  AND (SELECT AVG(w.weather_state) FROM Weather AS w
       WHERE w.country_id = c.country_id AND YEAR(w.day) = 2019 AND MONTH(w.day) = 11) < 25
notes:
## Intuition

Each country gets one label computed from one number: the average of its November 2019 readings. That is a filter (keep only November 2019 rows), a group per country with `AVG`, and a `CASE` that turns the average into a word. Countries without any November reading never form a group, so they drop out on their own.

## Approach

1. CTE `november`: keep rows with `day` between `'2019-11-01'` and `'2019-11-30'`, group them by `country_id` and compute `avg_state`.
2. Join `november` to `Countries` to turn the id into `country_name`.
3. A `CASE` maps the average to `'Cold'` (at most 15), `'Hot'` (at least 25) or `'Warm'`, named `weather_type`.

## Example 1, step by step

`november` holds one row per country with a reading in the month:

- USA (2): only 15 on 2019-11-01 counts (the October rows are filtered out), average 15 → Cold.
- Australia (3): (-2 + 0 + 3) / 3 ≈ 0.33 → Cold.
- China (5): (16 + 18 + 21) / 3 ≈ 18.33 → Warm.
- Peru (7): only 25 on 2019-11-28; the December rows are dropped, average 25 → Hot.
- Morocco (8): (25 + 27 + 31) / 3 ≈ 27.67 → Hot.

Spain (9) has readings only in October and December, so it has no row in `november` and is not reported.

## Complexity

- Time: O(W) to filter and group W weather rows, plus O(C) to join the C countries by id.
- Space: O(C) for the per-country averages.

## Pitfalls

- Filtering with `MONTH(day) = 11` alone also counts November of other years; the year must be fixed too.
- The boundaries are inclusive: an average of exactly 15 is Cold and exactly 25 is Hot, so use `<=` and `>=`.
- Averaging before filtering (or putting the date test in `HAVING`) mixes October and December readings into the average.
- Starting from `Countries` with a left join would report countries without November data with a null average and the label `'Warm'`.

## Clauses

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `november` | one row per country with November 2019 readings: `country_id` and its average `avg_state` |
| `n` | alias of `november` in the final query |
| `c` | `Countries`, supplying `country_name` |
| `weather_type` | the `CASE` label: Cold, Hot or Warm |

narration.1: The november stage computes one average temperature per country.
narration.4: Only readings from 1 to 30 November 2019 take part, both ends included.
narration.5: Grouping by country makes AVG average each country's November readings.
narration.9: The CASE turns the average into the weather_type label.
narration.10: An average of at most 15, including exactly 15, is Cold.
narration.11: An average of 25 or more is Hot; anything strictly between 15 and 25 falls to Warm.
narration.14: The averages are the driving table, so countries without November data never appear.
narration.15: Joining Countries on country_id swaps the id for the country's name.
